decision.active: Entire required SSI engine plus principal skills/competencies and their dependency closure
decision.archive: Historical installations, consolidation copies, inactive variants and workshop material subject to native retention and active dependency checks

active_components: Native SCC and versioned mission contracts
Router V10/S10 and authoritative skill registers
Active Research Memory and actor identity
CONTINUUM, queues, unfinished missions, checkpoints, recovery
Evidence/Notary chain heads, verification and retained history references
Permissions and existing communication with Robert/CODEX/CORE24
invariants: Preserve IDs, actor identity, versions, provenance, ACL, executable bodies, dependencies and evidence links
Do not promote skills from catalog labels, Python AST validity or synthetic test PASS
Do not merge mutable actor state solely because bytes match
Do not choose canonical skills by file time or copy count
Active skill dependencies must be available without NOUT1 or the skill must explicitly remain archive-dependent
Archive classification is not deletion or an independently verified backup

storage.acceptance_formula: active unpacked payload + required runtime/data not already counted + OS/container overhead + growth reserve <= available disk budget; count each item once
storage.model_weight_policy: Use shared CORE24 model service; do not duplicate weights on Director without a specific requirement

skills_audit.evidence_kind: Operator-provided audit archives reviewed locally; no fresh execution on MSI

scc.target_connection: SCC -> native mission contract -> Router V10/S10 -> Research Memory / MultiQuant adapter -> executor -> Evidence

Close dependencies and measure unpacked and allocated size
Stage without NOUT1; verify mission, restart and bounded recovery

Separate actual runtime/state requirements from synthetic fixtures
Map existing SCC contracts and identify missing bindings without inventing a replacement grammar

public_policy: Sanitized decisions, results and limits only; no private code, source payloads, databases, credentials, host addresses or private filesystem paths
